clue.text: Send off to see little girl's bit of land

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana, so a little girl's is DI'S
a patch is a small plot of ground

explanation.surface: Someone is sent off to inspect a young girl's garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch a letter or messenger is to send it on its way.

clue.text: Tree for lovers' meeting?

parts.note: a romantic appointment is a date, and a palm with clasped hands suits courting couples, so the tree's name splits into two lovers' words

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking which tree is a lovers' trysting spot; the name's halves are a romantic appointment and the hand they hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree is the palm that bears dates, grown across North Africa and the Middle East.

clue.text: Cricketer drinks — appearing on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the drinks come above the edge

parts.note: shorts are small measures of spirits
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A cricketer has a few drinks and ends up teetering on the brink.
explanation.walkthrough: A short slip is a close fielding position beside the batsman in cricket, and also the fielder in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short slip is a fielder stationed close behind the batsman, so a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Agitated in a prison compound

indicators.note: the two pieces are put together into one word, as a compound joins parts

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone is getting worked up inside a jail compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means stirred up, in a state of excitement or bustle.

clue.text: Officer suffered, getting trained

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
ached means felt pain

explanation.surface: An officer went through pain while being drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be coached is to have been taught or drilled by an instructor.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation in Swiss Cottage

definitions.meaning: a hut or cabin at a holiday camp
a wooden house of the Alps

explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is also a district of north London, which makes the capitals look like a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday camps let small cabins of that name, and the word first meant a timber Alpine farmhouse.

clue.text: Author set fruit tree before end of June

indicators.note: the tree comes ahead of the final letter in the answer

parts.note: the hawthorn bears haws, small red fruits

indicators.note: the last letter of the word June is taken

explanation.surface: A writer plants a fruit tree just before June is out.
explanation.walkthrough: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter; 'set' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a 19th-century American novelist.

clue.text: Craft one gets in old railway

indicators.note: the numeral boards the railway, so it goes inside the railway's letters

parts.note: LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, a pre-nationalisation British company
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vessel that once travelled on an old railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Slope, for example, in hill chap's name for it

indicators.note: the reversal sits within the hill's letters

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
the word slope is poles spelt backwards, so it is an example of a rev, short for reversal

explanation.surface: A slope on a hill gives a man his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for it' points back to the hill: the man's name is the wordplay. The trick is that 'Slope' is itself a reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a common male first name of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Animals from South America — many all upset?

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole run of pieces is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: Are animals from South America all overturned in large numbers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole run S A M ALL around; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are domesticated pack animals of the Andes.

clue.text: Spotted flycatcher?

parts.note: the spotted flycatcher is a bird, but read literally it is a speckled creature that catches flies, as a freshwater fish rising to anglers' flies does

explanation.walkthrough: The spotted flycatcher is a real songbird, which is the false path; the fish is speckled and snaps at mayflies.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown fish is spotted and feeds on insects at the surface, hence anglers' fly fishing.

clue.text: Toleration required to break a lance with cartoonist

indicators.note: the cartoonist's name breaks into the spear's letters, splitting them apart

parts.note: David Low was a famous political cartoonist for the London Evening Standard

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with a jousting lance being snapped by a satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: LOW goes after AL of A LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a tolerance or concession, as in making allowances for someone.

clue.text: Spare them pieces of cloth

indicators.note: the two words are broken into pieces and their letters put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A request to spare some scraps of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a heavy ribbed ribbon or woollen fabric used for waistbands and overcoats.

clue.text: Marx didn't talk when shot

parts.note: shot means filmed: the Marx brother who stayed mute on screen and played the harp

explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl and 'shot' suggests a gun; it means filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo was the silent Marx Brother, communicating by mime and a horn.

clue.text: Religious follower backed everything master put out

indicators.note: the master is stretched out to take in the other piece

parts.note: a lord is a master

indicators.note: the word for everything is written backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A disciple turned his back on everything his master threw out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' makes LLA, which 'put out' places inside LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English reformer.

clue.text: What soldier may come to heed

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier comes to stiff upright posture at command, and taking notice of something is also paying it mind.

clue.text: Southern transport stopped working

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Southern Region lorries came to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who struck went on strike, downing tools.

clue.text: Invent a true blend of liqueur

parts.note: to coin a word is to invent it

indicators.note: the letters of a true are mixed together

explanation.surface: Instructions to create a new mix of liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Argued like somebody overdrawn, apparently

indicators.note: the three pieces only seem to give the meaning, their letters being rearranged

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
as means like
one means a person

explanation.surface: Someone argued like a person with an overdraft, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like somebody overdrawn' reads as RED AS ONE; 'apparently' admits those letters only approximate the answer and must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reasoned is to have argued logically.

clue.text: A way youth leader displays indifference

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader shows no enthusiasm for the route.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern.

clue.text: Colour liable to run?

explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like dye spreading in the wash; it means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a primary hue and also, informally, cowardice.

clue.text: Abstract picture finally appears nice

parts.note: a precis is a summary or abstract

indicators.note: the final letter of the word picture

explanation.surface: An abstract painting turns out pleasant after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract' looks like art; it is a summary. 'nice' means exact, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fine or exact, as in a nice distinction.

clue.text: Player from one Cricket Club in another game

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the game's letters

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A player from a cricket club turns out for a different sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo player is an orchestral member, and the instrument's name stands for the player.

clue.text: Vessel made of part of tree, say

indicators.note: the word for the tree's covering is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: bark is a tree's outer layer

explanation.surface: A boat built from a section of tree, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a three-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Crime of penniless clergyman

indicators.note: P stands for penny, and the clergyman loses it

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A churchman's offence was being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Possible 3-step

indicators.note: the letters of that answer could possibly form another word when rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer at 3 down

explanation.surface: A dance called the three-step, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is 3-down, ASTIR, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight.

clue.text: Delicate material tears badly in mangles

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric

indicators.note: the word tears is jumbled badly

explanation.surface: Fine lace is ripped badly when put through a wringer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangles' suggests laundry wringers; it is a verb, tears up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or cut flesh roughly, like mangling it.

clue.text: Scholar is Hindu that'll provide the answer

definitions.text: Scholar is Hindu that'll provide the answer

indicators.note: the clue says the words themselves will supply the letters, which run inside them

explanation.surface: A learned Hindu will be able to tell you.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or seer, a learned holy man.

clue.text: As if mood alters character of Hugo

parts.note: quasi is Latin for as if

indicators.note: the letters of mood are changed in order

explanation.surface: A mood shift seems to change a Victor Hugo figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasimodo is the hunchback bell-ringer in Victor Hugo's Notre-Dame de Paris.

clue.text: Polish female quarters

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A Polish woman's living area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' as a nationality is the false path; it means lustre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft gloss or shine, the result of polishing.

clue.text: Head off swimmer going the wrong way

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off the front of the fish

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Stop a fish heading the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: To be erring is to stray from the right course.

clue.text: Wife involved in pile-up, almost dead

indicators.note: the wife is caught up inside the heap

parts.note: a mound is a heap
a rib is a jocular term for a wife, from Eve made of Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A wife caught in a motorway crash is close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means at the point of death.
